step0_classification.evidence: core switch fans 2 edges to neighbours (core->web 10 GbE, core->cache 25 GbE) and two separate relations converge on the cache tier (core->cache 25 GbE, web->cache session) and on the DB tier (web->db queries, cache->db fill), which the source's fixed constraint requires kept separate.
step0_classification.secondary_recipe_applied: none. The spine wan->fw->core->web keeps one stage per hop, which is the flow-chain corridor habit, but no flow-chain lever (short single-stage ranks) was needed beyond the source's own order.
tie_breakers_considered: density (E=7 > N=6) rules out flow-chains: the relation count exceeds the node count, so the graph is not one-relation-per-node.
no disconnected worlds and no source-named bus between them, so placement-planes does not apply.
no addresses, ports, AS numbers or uncertainty qualifiers, so identity-probe-maps does not apply.
no double-arrowhead targets, no dots-forbidden statement, and the source explicitly asks for live dots (line 5), so redundant-fabrics does not apply.
no wide fan out of one state and no phase ordering, so lifecycle-machines does not apply.
the skill's own family table names `network` as a service-mesh case; the source confirms it with a 2-edge fan around the core switch.
step0_classification.paired_relation_note: This source has no true anti-parallel pair (no request/response between the same two boxes). What it has is a paired inbound relation: cache receives core->cache (25 GbE) and web->cache (session); db receives web->db (queries) and cache->db (fill). Both pairs are drawn as two distinct edges with distinct labels and distinct ports in the SAME view; nothing was merged into one bidirectional arrow.

rank_pins_layers.reason: the source's own order is already the engine's longest-path rank order (wan, fw, core, web, cache, db), so pinning would add no information; the skill prefers omitting `layers`.

minlen.reason: no source fact describes a corridor that needs extra rank gap; minlen would only inflate the extent past 47 rows.

trunks.reason: the source states independent physical links with their own speeds (1 GbE, 10 GbE, 10 GbE, 25 GbE) and application relations, not one shared bus; a trunk would fake a shared corridor and merge locally independent links. No source-stated bus exists, so 'check.txt' prints an empty `trunks:` line.

label_slot.source_fact: the labels are the source's link speeds and application relations (1 GbE, 10 GbE, 10 GbE, 25 GbE, session, queries, fill) and must stay beside their own route; with rank-gap slots alone the same spec measured extent 29x67 (attempts-log label v1-attempt2-tb), over the 47-row target. label_slot moves each label into a side gutter: extent 27x45, 7/7 placed, 0 ambiguous owners.

motion.source_fact: source line 5: live dots flowing along the lines, dot direction = traffic flow; the Task asks for slow, sparse motion.
motion.applied: flow: true on all 7 edges (constant default 0.5 cells per 100 ms step - the slowest mode the renderer offers), dots: 1 on each edge (one dot per route = sparse). No numeric flow rate, no same-arrival timing: the source gives no rate and the fixed constraint forbids implying that motion speed measures the link speed.
motion.speed_labels: 1 GbE / 10 GbE / 25 GbE stay text labels in gutters; every route animates at the same rate, so no route is faster than another and motion encodes nothing about speed.
